slots.title: Brent down 1.3% after energy ceasefire headline
slots.body:
Brent crude (BZUSD) finished at 103.31, down 1.3% (-1.41) from the prior close of 104.72.

CNBC tied the move to Trump’s statement that Russia and Ukraine will not target each other’s energy facilities.

The U.S. oil ETF $USO closed up 0.4% at 148.20 — a smaller move than Brent in the cross-asset snapshot.

What energy headlines are you tracking this week?

slots.title: 10-year Treasury at 5.2% as Fed voices linger
slots.body:
U.S. Treasury yields in the FMP set dated 2026-10-09:

- 2-year: 4.8%
- 10-year: 5.2%
- 2s10s spread: 0.44

The 30-year printed at 5.6%; the 20-year at 5.7%.

The Wall Street Journal reported Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack saying that when companies still have pricing power, she worries rates are not yet high enough to tame inflation — the Fed’s job is to keep prices stable over time.

Seeking Alpha’s weekend piece flagged upcoming CPI and PPI as near-term catalysts for rates and valuations; those prints are not in today’s FMP calendar block.

Where do you look first — the 10-year level or the 2s10s spread?

slots.title: U.S. cash session — Oct. 12, 2026
slots.body:
The S&P 500 closed up 0.6% at 7,811.54 (+46.18 points), with a session range of 7,779.34 to 7,820.57 in the injected index feed.

The Nasdaq Composite rose 0.6% to 27,366.17 (+172.83), and the Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 0.8% to 51,654.95 (+423.31).

The Russell 2000 added 0.5% to 2,806.98, while the CBOE Volatility Index ($VIX) fell 3.7% to 14.84 (session low 14.77).

Sector averages on the injected Nasdaq table for 2026-10-12 put Utilities up 2.8% and Healthcare up 2.1%, with Consumer Cyclical +1.3% and Real Estate +1.0%; Industrials averaged -0.9% and Technology -0.6%, Communication Services -0.5%, and Energy -0.2%.

Among megacaps in the same snapshot, $MSFT rose 2.4% to 535.07, $ORCL gained 4.7% to 141.53, and $AMZN added 3.3% to 262.43; $TSLA was up 2.1% to 382.70.

$AAPL slipped 1.1% to 336.64 (day low 330.70), and $NVDA edged down 0.5% to 229.28; $META was off 0.3% to 718.67.

Healthcare names in the injected set included:
- $UNH +2.3% to 379.30
- $JNJ +1.9% to 261.44
- $ABBV +1.5% to 276.47

with $ABBV’s printed high at 277.60.

The most active list in the data showed $T down 9.8% to 22.18 and $VZ down 8.7% to 41.65 on heavy attention names alongside smaller-cap actives.

Treasury yields in the injected curve dated 2026-10-09 showed the 10-year at 5.2%, the 2-year at 4.8%, and a 2s10s spread of 0.44 percentage points.

Gold futures in the cross-asset block rose 0.2% to 4,223.50; Bitcoin ($BTCUSD) was down 0.3% to 83,391.57, and the dollar proxy $UUP ticked up 0.1% to 29.02.

Overseas indexes in the package included FTSE 100 +1.1% to 10,552.05 and the Hang Seng flat at 24,217.00; Brent crude finished down 1.3% at 103.33 after weekend headlines on energy-facility targeting.

The injected U.S. calendar for the date listed Columbus Day (impact none), an IMF meeting, and a scheduled Fed Hammack speech; the earnings calendar array was empty and no macro print fields were attached to this close bundle.

slots.title: Fastenal reports Tuesday with $0.34 EPS est.
slots.body:
$FAST reports Tuesday, Oct. 14.

EPS estimate: $0.34.

Revenue estimate: about $2.44 billion.

Fastenal sells fasteners and MRO supplies into factories and job sites, so the line items often track capex and construction activity before broader industrials report.

Results land in the same week as large bank and inflation prints, but the customer mix is manufacturing and onsite consumption, not trading desks.

slots.title: Schwab and Interactive Brokers report Wednesday
slots.body:
Two large public brokers report Wednesday, Oct. 15.

- $SCHW — EPS estimate $1.66; revenue estimate about $7.20 billion
- $IBKR — EPS estimate $0.67; revenue estimate about $1.86 billion

Schwab skews toward mass-market investing and advice; Interactive Brokers skews toward active and international traders.

Both filings break out interest earned on client cash versus fees and commissions — the split that moves when short-term rates and client behavior shift.

Same calendar day also carries wholesale inflation and retail sales at 12:30–1:30 p.m.
ET, so the session stacks macro prints with brokerage P&L detail.

When you read a broker quarter, do you start with net interest income or with client asset flows?
